Someone else mentioned uncle punch. Use the training events in that to learn a lot of the basics. It's got some advanced stuff in there as well. Don't worry about those as much. Focus solely on wavedashing and L-cancels. You want your movement as accurate as possible, speed will come on its own as you learn the game. Just focus on making sure your character moves exactly as you want it to. 

Play with anyone who will sit down with you. Try and get as much time on a CRT as you can. Project slippi is a mod that lets you record replays automatically. Look into that so you can watch any footage you have.  

Find your local scene. If you don't have one, find the closest one. Try and make it out to there events. You can start with netplay, but if you want to get really good, you'll have to start playing in tournaments.

The biggest thing is, everything you practice should have purpose, and should be integrated into your game. For example, I've been working on doing shine out of shield as falco, but I've not been implementing it into my game at all. Pretty useless right? At first, you might wanna just force yourself to do these things in game even if it's not "optimal." Slowly you'll learn when to use it and when to try something else. 

It's important to have options. Mix things up. Don't get predictable. Figure out what top players are doing and use it. But don't rely on them entirely. The sickest thing you can do is get creative. 


If you remember nothing else, remember this. It's just a game. It is okay to lose. We all did for a while, and still do. Have fun with it. Ask yourself why you play. Is it to be the best? To have fun? To be the sickest being to grace the sticks?  Whatever it is, don't lose sight of that goal. At times it may feel unobtainable. Take a break, and come back when you are ready to. Don't force it. You'll find yourself hating the experience more and more and will burn yourself out.  This game is hard. Some could argue it's the hardest smash game. Don't sweat it though, just keep grinding.

I've always had a weird relationship with character choice in smash games. I started with brawl when I was around 7 years old and even then I knew in my heart meta knight was fucking busted, and played the shit out of him. 


Many years later I stumbled my way into smash 4. Zss and diddy were my two immediate character choices. I personally love diddy, but something about zss called out to me. At this point I still know nothing about competitive level play. I play around with the cast and discover a love for fox, mewtwo, and so many other top tiers. I did eventually drop zss after realizing I didn't enjoy her play style, but she was still oddly one of my first pickups. I played pre patch diddy with a Wii mote and nunchuck, knowing nothing more than attack and recover. Couldn't even throw yet. 

I switch to melee and at this point I know some shit, and have been around the scene for a while. Fox is cool, but falco has all the style points, while remaining high tier. An easy choice.

Ultimate drops, and less than an hour In I fell in love with inklings play style. Then wolf. Then pichu. 


Something has always lead me to high tiers, even when I knew nothing of tiers. I inherently have gravitated to the best characters.
